title: SPEC-04 reverter + lifecycle: write-ahead inverse, TTL ownership, detached reverter, boot reconcile, kill switch
reasoning: The single most dangerous failure mode is a fault that outlives its run. The inverse is recorded BEFORE the fault lands, a separate process owns the TTL and survives the CLI, boot reconcile marks leftovers `stuck`, and one kill switch reverts everything. Proven shape to imitate: `systemd-run --user --scope -p RuntimeMaxSec=` and the netns revert verified live in probe/RESULTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: AC-4 (revert is measured, not asserted), AC-5 (CLI kill -9 mid-hold still reverts at TTL), AC-6 (revert --all within 2s with per-fault proof).

title: SPEC-05 verdict engine: vocabulary, probes/assertions, integrity oracle, control run, timing model
reasoning: The verdict vocabulary is the anti-false-green device: no_op, aborted, corrupted, flaky, void exist precisely because a green-but-meaningless run would otherwise report recovered (the exact failure of the legacy five cells, PRD §2.1). Timing model t_landed/t_symptom/t_detect/t_recover is what turns a verdict into a number the fleet can compare across runs.
acceptance_criteria: AC-13 (no verdict rests on the fault's own exit code), AC-15 (missing integrity oracle forbids `recovered`), AC-16 (control run must be green else the experiment is `void`), AC-9.

title: SPEC-13 isolation contract + enforcement: mischief's own work runs on an ephemeral sanctioned host, never the main host; protected targets refuse at resolution
reasoning:
SPEC-13 — the isolation contract, and the mechanical check that enforces it.

WHY THIS IS A P0 SPEC AND NOT A PARAGRAPH. The PRD §7 already states the doctrine (no default target, never its own process tree, protected targets, load gate, scratch-only file faults). What it does NOT state is where MISCHIEF ITSELF is allowed to run, and doctrine without a mechanical check is decorative — the fleet has already been burned twice this week by exactly that shape: a net-drop cell that ran an iptables rule it had no privilege to apply and logged "attempted, not proven", and a battery that printed "cells: all" while running zero cells. Both were doc-vs-behaviour gaps, not code bugs.

THE RULE THIS SPEC ADDS. Mischief's own development, selftest and battery runs happen on an EPHEMERAL BUNKER INSTANCE, never on the fleet's main host. The main host carries the scheduler, the gateway, the memory daemon and ~366 live lanes; a fault injector pointed at it by accident is not a bug, it is an outage. So the default target for mischief's own work is a bunker agent, and the main host is a PROTECTED TARGET that refuses.

THE MECHANISM (this is the spec's real content, not the prose):
 1. A host admits mischief only when it carries an explicit SANCTION marker (file + env), which the main host does not carry. Absence is a REFUSAL, not a warning — fail closed.
 2. The refusal names the host and the missing marker, exits non-zero, and writes nothing.
 3. The protected list (scheduler, gateway, memory daemon, PID 1, kernel threads, mischief's own tree + reverter) is evaluated at TARGET RESOLUTION, before any actuator is selected, so a protected target cannot be reached by picking a different primitive.
 4. The scope ladder (§7) is a spec, not a comment: L0 scratch is the only unconditional tier; L1 needs rootless proof; L2 needs the helper allowlist; L3 the docker API; L4 the simulator; L5 real cloud is opt-in and refused in v0.1 without --allow-real.
 5. The load gate reads PSI/loadavg and REFUSES to land a fault on an already-saturated host. A fault injector that adds load to a struggling host manufactures the incident it claims to observe.

CONSEQUENCE TO SPECIFY, because the two rules interact: a bunker agent is unprivileged (measured: uid 1004, no passwordless sudo, `unshare -rn` fails at the uid_map write), so the L2/L3 primitives CANNOT be exercised there. The spec must therefore name, per tier, the sanctioned test environment — and say plainly which primitives are L0/L1-only in v0.1 because no fleeting sanctioned host can run them. A primitive that cannot be tested on a sanctioned host does not ship.
acceptance_criteria: AC: the isolation contract is enforced, not described. (1) Running mischief's own selftest on a host WITHOUT the sanction marker REFUSES: exit non-zero, a message naming the host and the missing marker, and zero bytes written to the target. (2) The same command on a sanctioned scratch host proceeds. (3) A protected target (the scheduler's own process, the gateway, PID 1, mischief's own tree) cannot be reached by naming a different primitive — the refusal happens at target resolution, before any actuator is chosen. (4) The load gate refuses on a saturated host. Evidence: the four transcripts, including the refusal exits, plus a test that FAILS if the marker check is neutered (a doc-only guarantee must not be able to pass).

title: Bunker test plane for mischief's own development: agent at tick start, evidence pulled back, agent destroyed, zero main-host residue
reasoning:
The busted assumption worth naming: a foreman lane runs its commands on the host the scheduler lives on. For every other project that is fine — they build and test their own code. For a fault injector it is not fine, because the work IS the fault, and the worker's own cwd sits next to the scheduler, the gateway and the memory daemon.

So mischief's lane needs a TEST PLANE, not a promise:
  - every tick that exercises a primitive runs on an ephemeral bunker agent
  - the agent is created at tick start and destroyed at tick end (or on a bounded TTL, whichever is shorter)
  - nothing lands on the main host: no scratch dirs, no armed faults, no leftover agents
  - the evidence (journal + the landed-proof counters) is PULLED BACK before destroy, so the tick's report is produced from artifacts, not from the agent's memory
  - an agent that cannot be obtained is a recorded SKIP with a named reason, never a silent pass — the fleet has a fresh precedent for why (a QA lane reported a full battery from an agent that had already been destroyed)

WHAT TO REUSE, NOT REBUILD: the fleet already has three working planes. bunker-qa.sh (one-shot battery, JIT agent, toolchain bootstrap, collect, destroy), bunker-soak.sh (long-duration soak with a fault ladder and a verdict engine), and gauntlet (~/gauntlet — the standalone Go fault battery with 16 cells and a jolt relay, proven against trouble on a scratch port with no bunker). This row is the integration, and its first job is to decide which of the three is the substrate rather than inventing a fourth.

THE HARD PART, stated so it is not discovered mid-build: `mischief`'s L0/L1 primitives (signals, systemd-run --user scopes, the LD_PRELOAD shim, the seccomp supervisor, the userspace proxy) are exactly the set a bunker agent CAN run — measured, the shim and user-scope limits work rootless. The L2/L3 set (netns+netem, dm/loop, freezer, docker) cannot, so those need either a sanctioned non-fleet box or a container with NET_ADMIN, and the spec must say which. Do not let the plane's convenience silently shrink the catalogue: name the primitives the plane cannot exercise and file that as its own gap.
acceptance_criteria: AC: (1) One command takes a clean sanctioned host from nothing to evidence: obtain agent -> ship repo -> build (no `make` dependency on a bare agent; it has no C toolchain) -> run the L0/L1 selftest -> pull the journal and the landed-proof counters back -> destroy the agent. (2) After it returns, the main host shows NO residue: no scratch state, no armed faults, no surviving agent, and the evidence is present locally. (3) An unobtainable agent is reported as a recorded SKIP with a named reason and is never rendered as a pass. (4) The set of primitives the plane CANNOT exercise (the L2/L3 set needing privileges a bunker agent lacks) is enumerated in the spec with the sanctioned environment for each, not left implied. Evidence: one full transcript plus the main-host residue check before/after.

title: Scheduler readiness: register the mischief project (DB + the fleet configuration pin) and derive the foreman + satellite set incl. the battery/chaos satellite
reasoning:
Scheduler readiness: register the project, then the satellites — with the isolation constraint attached to the lane itself.

WHAT "READY FOR THE SCHEDULER" ACTUALLY REQUIRES (derived, not guessed):
 - a row in the `projects` table AND a `[[projects]]` stanza in ~/.hermes/the fleet configuration. The toml is the DURABLE pin — a policy regen writes enabled rows only, so enabling in the DB alone does not survive.
 - ONE enabled lane per workdir (the API 409s a second, case-insensitively). `<workdir>` is free today; verify before registering rather than after.
 - `namespace_id`, `deliver` and the model/provider pair, matching the fleet's convention. `mischief`'s the knowledge store namespace now exists (created 2026-09-28), so `namespace_id` has something real to point at.
 - the lane's WORKDIR is where the board is read: `.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl`. 21 rows, 19 dispatchable, validated clean.
 - the lane's consumers read `status == "pending"` and nothing else. Every row filed for this project must land pending; a row left in any other spelling is invisible to the foreman. This is measured, not asserted: the scheduler's own board_awareness counts only pending, and the fleet gate's allowed set is (pending, in_progress, complete, duplicate).

THE SATELLITE SET — derive it from the fleet's convention rather than inventing it: a primary plus the standard satellites (`-qa`, `-sync`, `-pm`, `-docs`, `-releng`, `-review`), each in its OWN namespace, all reading the primary's board. The one that is genuinely distinctive here is the CHAOS/BATTERY satellite: it runs the project's fault matrix on a cadence and files findings, and it is the satellite that makes this project self-testing. It is also the satellite with the highest blast radius, so it inherits MSF-020's isolation contract in full — it may not run a fault on the scheduler's own host.

THE ORDERING TRAP, stated because it will otherwise be discovered the expensive way: MSF-017 already files the -chaos satellite as "M6, P3" (after the whole build). That is too late. The lane should exist EARLY and run a deliberately tiny matrix (the primitives that already work rootless on a scratch target), because a lane that only ever runs after the build is finished has never been exercised as a lane — and the fleet's standing lesson is that a pipeline is proven by its destination, not by its configuration.
acceptance_criteria: AC: (1) `mischief` appears as an enabled project in the fleet API and a `[[projects]]` stanza in the fleet configuration, and survives a policy regen with the enable intact. (2) The primary lane dispatches, reads .coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl, and moves a pending row to in_progress and back — proven by a real tick, not by configuration. (3) The satellite set is derived from the DB (`projects WHERE name LIKE 'mischief%'` plus their workdirs), not hand-listed, and each satellite reads the primary's board. (4) The battery/chaos satellite runs a deliberately tiny matrix against a scratch target and files at least one real finding. (5) No lane in the project runs a fault on the scheduler's own host — verified by the isolation check of MSF-020, not by inspection of intent.
